measurement.NA: not one of the six constructs

author.name: Sacha Altay
author.affiliation: Department of Political Science, University of Zurich

construct.def: What the percentage is a share of. The denominator sets the construct, never the topic or what is counted in the numerator.

levels.EXPOSURE: the share of a person's actual information diet (visits, views, time) that is misinformation, from behavioural records
levels.REACH: the share of people who encountered misinformation at least once, from behavioural records
levels.RECALL: the share of people who say they have seen or shared misinformation, from surveys
levels.SHARING: the share of shares, posts or links that carry misinformation, from behavioural records
levels.CONTENT: the share of items in a sampled corpus (posts, videos, articles) classified as misinformation
levels.CONCENTRATION: the share of all misinformation activity accounted for by the most active users or sources
levels.QUALITY: a source or content quality rating that is not a veracity judgement; never pooled with prevalence
levels.OTHER: a composition or other quantity outside the six constructs; never pooled

measurement.def: The kind of evidence, derived from the construct.

levels.CONTENT_CODING: researchers, fact-checkers or classifiers judged sampled items
levels.BEHAVIOURAL: records of what people actually saw, visited or shared
levels.NA: quality scores and other quantities outside the six constructs

ground_truth.def: Who decided what counted as misinformation.

levels.researcher_coding: the authors or trained coders, following a codebook
levels.domain_list: a list of unreliable sources such as NewsGuard or the Grinberg lists; everything from a listed source counts
levels.self_report: the respondents' own judgement of what they saw
levels.fact_checker: verdicts of professional fact-checkers or an expert panel, claim by claim
levels.classifier: an automated classifier or suspicion score

classification_level.def: Whether misinformation was judged per source or per item. Claim-level judgement finds several times more than source-level.

levels.claim_level: each item, post or claim was classified on its own content
levels.source_level: whole outlets or accounts were classified and everything they published counts; a lower bound on false items

breadth.def: How wide the veracity net is, where the definition sets a per-item standard.

levels.false: verifiably false against a ground truth
levels.misleading: false or misleading, including manipulated or missing-context content
levels.not_stated: no per-item veracity standard: typically source lists and quality ratings

denom_class.def: The universe the percentage is a share of. If the percentage were 100%, what would that mean?

levels.population: a defined group of people: respondents, panellists, users
levels.all_media: everything a person consumed, news and non-news
levels.news_diet: all the news a person consumed, on any topic
levels.topical: content on one issue, typically a keyword or hashtag corpus
levels.curated_sample: a hand-picked set with no natural total, such as the most-shared posts or fact-check-seeded items
levels.single_source: one account, channel, outlet or platform feature
levels.n/a: no denominator by construction: concentration estimates
levels.not_reported: the fused class was not filled on this row; its scope is coded separately

levels.panel_trace: a behavioural panel: web tracking, browsing or voter-file panels
levels.full_census: a full platform census or firehose
levels.curated_seed: a set seeded from fact-checks or a known-misinformation list
levels.purposive: a purposive selection by the researchers
levels.random_platform: a random or representative sample of the platform
levels.curated_business_pages: a curated set of business pages

platform_norm.def: The platform or medium, with the papers' 274 spellings collapsed. For surveys it is the frame of the question, not a measured source.

levels.survey: a survey question, not a measured platform
levels.web_cross_platform: browsing or tracking data across the web
levels.other: a platform outside the named list

topic.def: The subject of the misinformation studied, one code per study. COVID vaccines count as COVID-19; a whole-diet or domain-list study is general news.

levels.general_news: no single subject: whole diets, domain lists, general news

country_scope.def: How many countries the estimate covers.

rob.def: Risk of bias on the Hoy prevalence instrument, adapted for this review (Methods 4.7). LOW: 0 to 2 items at high risk with the two design items low. MODERATE: 3 to 5, or one design item high. HIGH: 6 or more, or both design items high.

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Platforms studied, by construct. Bars are the share of that construct's studies that cover the platform, against a track showing all of them; study counts are in brackets and the eight most covered platforms are shown per construct. A study counts once in every platform it names, so bars within a panel sum to more than k. Supplementary Note A5 gives the counting rule and the ground-truth and country breakdowns.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Topics studied, by construct. Bars are the share of that construct's studies on each topic, with study counts in brackets.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Prevalence estimates by construct. Study-level medians with 95% confidence intervals from a study-cluster bootstrap (2,000 resamples).

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: What drives the estimate. Study-level median prevalence by measurement type, sampling frame, ground-truth source, construct, and identification level, over the studies in the main analysis set that contribute to the six prevalence constructs. n = studies at that level, and the figure beside each band heading is that band's total. The bands rest on different totals because a study whose value for a moderator is not coded is omitted from that band only.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Concentration of misinformation versus news in general. In each pair the left column is the user population and the right column all of the activity, with the share accounted for by the top 1% of users filled in. Both columns are drawn to scale: the top 1% band is 1% of the height of the people column. Left: the study-level median share of misinformation activity accounted for by the top 1% of users, across the 5 studies reporting exactly that threshold (range 37-80%). Right: the median of 6 comparison estimates of general-news activity, from the 4 panels that report both quantities (range 30-43%). The two medians come from different sets of studies.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.caption: PRISMA flow diagram. Records identified, screened, retrieved and included, with the corpus repair shown as its own identification stream.

figures.label: Supplementary Fig. 1
figures.caption: Ground truth by construct: who decided what counted as misinformation. Same form as Figure 1.

figures.label: Supplementary Fig. 2
figures.caption: Countries studied, by construct. Same form as Figure 1; a study counts once in every country label it carries.
